title: U.S. House · California's 14th Congressional District
area: Southern Alameda County, including Hayward, Fremont, Union City, Newark, and Pleasanton.

context.text: This seat was previously held by Eric Swalwell, who resigned on April 13, 2026. A special election was held to fill the vacancy for the remainder of the term: Aisha Wahab defeated Melissa Hernandez, 53.1%-46.9%, in the special general election on August 18, 2026. The two also advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary for the regular, full-term seat, with Wahab taking 38.3% and Hernandez 17.2% of the vote. As of September 7, 2026, Hernandez had raised about $1.99 million and Wahab about $421,000, according to FEC filings cited by Ballotpedia.

candidates.name: Aisha Wahab
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 special general election, 53.1%-46.9%, and also advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary for the regular term.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for California's 14th Congressional District (since August 2026); previously California State Senator, District 10 (2022-2026)

summary.text: Aisha Wahab is the Democratic incumbent representing California's 14th Congressional District, having won a special election in August 2026 to fill the seat vacated by Eric Swalwell. A former Hayward City Council member and California state senator, she was the first Afghan American woman elected to public office in the United States (2018) and the first Afghan American elected to the California Legislature (2022).

background.text: Born in New York, New York; lives in Hayward, California. Earned a B.A. in political science from San Jose State University, an MBA from California State University, East Bay, and a Ph.D. from the University of Southern California.
Career experience includes working as an IT manager, IT business consultant, and senior management analyst in finance.
Elected to the Hayward City Council in 2018, becoming mayor pro tempore in 2020; elected to the California State Senate, District 10, in 2022.

priorities.text: Says she is running to lower costs of housing, healthcare, childcare, groceries, gas, and utilities, and to take on corporate price-gouging and junk fees.
Says she will defend democracy, women's rights, civil rights, and immigrant families while supporting what she calls victim-first public safety.
Campaign site cites her Senate record delivering a $35 insulin cap, $300 million for first-time homebuyer down-payment assistance, and an expanded Renter's Tax Credit.

positions.summary: Campaign site says she expanded rent stabilization from 1,000 to 10,000 units on the Hayward City Council and expanded the state Renter's Tax Credit and tenant protections in the Senate.

Says she will push to increase funding for affordable, social, workforce, and starter housing, cut red tape, and speed up construction, while stopping Wall Street and private equity from buying single-family homes.
Says she delivered a $35 insulin cap in the state Senate and will push to protect Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, and SNAP from cuts or privatization in Congress.
Says she will push to expand paid family leave, universal childcare, after-school programs, and family tax relief.

record.text: Elected to the Hayward City Council in 2018 and to the California State Senate, District 10, in 2022, where she served as Assistant Majority Leader.
Won the special general election for California's 14th Congressional District on August 18, 2026, filling the vacancy left by Eric Swalwell.

candidates.name: Melissa Hernandez
candidates.currentRole: Member, Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) Board of Directors, District 5 (since 2024)
candidates.ballotNote: Lost the August 18, 2026 special general election to Wahab, 46.9%-53.1%; also advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary for the regular term.

summary.text: Melissa Hernandez is a Democratic candidate for California's 14th Congressional District who ran competitively against incumbent Aisha Wahab in both the August 2026 special election and the regular primary. She is the former mayor of Dublin, California and a current BART board director.

background.text: The daughter of migrant farmworkers and a Mexican immigrant father; raised two children as a single mother while working and putting herself through college.
Served as the first Latina mayor of Dublin, California.
Elected to the Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) Board of Directors, District 5, taking office in 2024; has served as BART Board President.
Ran unsuccessfully for the Alameda County Board of Supervisors, District 1, in the March 2020 primary.

priorities.text: Says lowering costs and expanding economic opportunity for working families, including housing, healthcare and childcare costs, will be her first priority in Congress.
Says she will push to give police, firefighters and emergency responders more training, staffing and resources while investing in mental-health crisis response and addiction treatment.
Says she will fight for real immigration reform, including a pathway to citizenship, while also supporting what she calls smart border security.

positions.summary: As mayor of Dublin, says she oversaw one of the region's largest housing expansions, including affordable housing for seniors and residents with disabilities alongside market-rate rentals; in Congress says she would work to lower housing costs and help first-time homebuyers.
Says she cut red tape and lowered building costs as mayor of Dublin, and in Congress would work to lower the cost of raw materials and provide incentives to build new housing.
Says she will protect and expand Medicare, restore insurance subsidies to reduce premium costs, and restore funding for health programs serving vulnerable families.

Says ICE's immigration enforcement is 'broken and out of control' and supports a pathway to citizenship for DREAMers and undocumented community members, while also saying she supports 'smart border security' and regional cooperation on migration.
positions.quote: ICE has become a symbol of an immigration system that's broken and out of control, and it needs fundamental reform. ... At the same time, Melissa supports smart border security and regional cooperation to address the root causes driving migration, not political stunts that put families in danger.

positions.summary: Supports a transition toward renewable energy sources and legislation to fully restore the Inflation Reduction Act's climate programs.
Supports expanding the Child Tax Credit, recruiting and better paying childcare workers, and paid family and medical leave.
Says she will fight to protect reproductive healthcare and restore reproductive freedom by supporting legislation like the Women's Health Protection Act.

record.text: Served as mayor of Dublin, California, where the city received a "Best Places to Live" designation during her tenure and expanded housing at multiple affordability levels.
Elected to the BART Board of Directors, District 5, taking office May 23, 2024; has served as BART Board President.
